title: Structural‐Functional Decoupling in Post‐Disturbance Forest Recovery: Canopy Cover Lags Hydrological Function Across Chinese Forests
content:
Abstract

Forest disturbance dynamics play a crucial role in terrestrial carbon sequestration and regional climate regulation. However, the coupled recovery processes of forest structure and function remain insufficiently understood. Here, we rigorously identified 930 forest recovery sites across China, each paired with undisturbed control sites. These sites represent large-scale, single-event disturbances (e.g., deforestation, wildfires) with varying life-history strategies. Using random forest with partial dependence plot analysis and partial least squares structural equation modeling, we analyzed the temporal response dynamics of structural (canopy cover) and functional (▵evapotranspiration (ET)) recovery in coniferous and broadleaf forests. Our results demonstrate that ΔET recovers significantly faster than canopy cover in both forest types, though this difference is more pronounced in coniferous forest than broadleaf forest. Spatial analysis revealed evident heterogeneity in these recovery patterns. Specifically, disturbed coniferous forest sites showed ΔET recovery in 6.8 ± 2.5 years versus 15.2 ± 1.6 years for canopy cover, while broadleaf forest sites required 8.2 ± 2.9 and 13.1 ± 1.7 years, respectively. This comprehensive analysis establishes a clear asynchrony between canopy cover and hydrological function recovery mechanisms. Leaf area index drives initial ET recovery and maintains ET influence even after canopy cover effects stabilize, independent of climatic and environmental factors. These findings reveal fundamental asynchronous recovery mechanisms between structural and functional indicators, further validated by GEDI data, providing critical theoretical support for region-specific forest restoration strategies.
